summary: The Military Occupancy Living Defense Act, or MOLD Act, requires the Secretary of Defense to establish and enforce health, safety, and habitability standards focused on relative humidity, ventilation, dampness, water intrusion, and mold for all military family housing. It mandates independent third-party inspections, specific remediation certifications, a 24/7 tenant complaint hotline and website, quarterly congressional reporting, and financial responsibility provisions for housing providers who fail to maintain habitable units.

affected_groups.effect: Receive enhanced housing health and safety protections, access to independent third-party inspections, a 24/7 complaint system, mandatory remediation or relocation within 30 days for failed inspections, and financial protections from private housing providers.
affected_groups.group: Members of the Armed Forces and their families residing in military family housing

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new Department of Defense environmental health standards, pay for third-party inspections, cover all costs associated with remediation, property loss, and tenant relocation for uninhabitable units, and face possible audits or suspension of housing-related bonuses for systemic noncompliance.
affected_groups.group: Privatized military housing providers and contractors

affected_groups.effect: Must issue safety standards, conduct and track independent inspections, maintain historical housing records, manage a 24/7 complaint system, and submit detailed quarterly and annual reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Defense and Military Housing Offices

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Defense to issue interim guidance on humidity, ventilation, dampness, and water intrusion within 180 days, followed by final standards within one year.
Mandates independent, certified third-party mold and environmental health inspections upon tenant turnover, receipt of complaints, and after remediation or structural repairs.

Requires privatized military housing providers to bear full financial responsibility for inspections, maintenance, mold remediation, relocation expenses, property loss, and basic allowance for housing refunds when units are uninhabitable.
Establishes a 24/7 tenant complaint hotline and website through the Defense Housing Feedback System and requires housing offices to respond within five business days.
Mandates that all maintenance personnel and mold remediators possess certifications from recognized nonprofit certifying bodies and follow standard professional remediation guidelines.
Imposes quarterly reporting requirements on military housing offices to the newly designated Chief Housing Officer, who must compile and submit reports and briefings to congressional committees.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations required to implement the inspection protocols, reporting systems, and administrative changes.
Exact penalties or enforcement mechanisms other than bonus suspensions for noncompliant private landlords.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Military Occupancy Living Defense Act, or MOLD Act, requires the Secretary of Defense to establish and enforce health, safety, and habitability standards focused on relative humidity, ventilation, dampness, water intrusion, and mold for all military family housing. It mandates independent third-party inspections, specific remediation certifications, a 24/7 tenant complaint hotline and website, quarterly congressional reporting, and financial responsibility provisions for housing providers who fail to maintain habitable units.
summary_detail.significance: The bill addresses environmental health and safety in military family housing by instituting mandatory independent inspections, standardized mold remediation protocols, strict timelines for hazard resolution, and financial accountability for private housing operators across approximately 700,000 members of the Armed Forces and their families.
